messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty — SEV2: metering.checkpoint_stall fired for prod-ingest (policy: ingest-lag-high). Alerts: oncall=jess_oncall, escalation=2

pagerduty: Alert created: PD-54321 — metering.checkpoint_stall. Service: Metering-Ingest. Triggered at 2026-03-14T02:12:01Z.

jess_oncall: acked the alert :white_check_mark:

jess_oncall: reading the runbook now. initial note: ingestion worker group 'ingest-a' reporting high commit backlog, checkpoint lag ~12m. token counts falling behind expected.

sam_sre: seeing similar in metrics. consumer lag increasing on kafka topic meter-events (partition 3/12). offsets stuck at 124, last processed offset 119?

carol_billing: are invoices at risk? any customers impacted already?

jess_oncall: unknown yet. putting a quick assessment: if checkpoint doesn't catch up within 30m, token-count windows for hourly aggregation will drop and could cause underbilling for some accounts.

olivia_support: flagged a customer message in #support about tokens not matching dashboard — sent to billing. pinging now to avoid duplicate comms.

sam_sre: attaching latest logs snippet from consumer group: ```
[ingest-a] 2026-03-14T02:10:45Z ERROR commit failed: OffsetOutOfRangeException partition=3 offset=125
[ingest-a] 2026-03-14T02:11:02Z WARN processed=119 lag=6 checkpoint_delay_ms=720000
[ingest-a] 2026-03-14T02:11:30Z INFO backpressure applied to producer connections
```

jess_oncall: looks like consumer is failing to commit; maybe retention or compaction issue? I’ll try manual restart of ingest-a consumer group. Will coordinate with sam before restart.

sam_sre: +1. before restart can you run `kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe --group metering-ingest-a --bootstrap-server pkb:9092` and paste offsets?

jess_oncall: running now...

jess_oncall: output:
```
GROUP           TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
metering-ingest  meter-events     3         119             125             6   consumer-abc
```

jess_oncall: ok confirmed current offset 119, log end 125. gap of 6. attempting restart of the ingest-a deployment (k8s) -> `kubectl rollout restart deployment/ingest-a -n metering`

sam_sre: watch the readiness probes. if restart fails, we should scale up a standby pool instead of full restart. fallback: scale deploy to 0 then back to 2.

jess_oncall: running restart...

incident-bot: Deployment ingest-a restarted by jess_oncall at 2026-03-14T02:16:40Z

sam_sre: logs show rejoin successful, consumer resumed processing. offsets progressing now: processed up to 123 within 90s.

jess_oncall: progress steady. lag down to 2. still monitoring.

carol_billing: any visible impact to token counts so far? can we run a quick reconciliation against the last stable checkpoint?

sam_sre: running a quick job to recompute expected token delta vs processed tokens for the last 10m. command: `python tools/reconcile_tokens.py --from 2026-03-14T01:50 --to 2026-03-14T02:10 --env prod`

sam_sre: reconcile job shows processed tokens behind expected by ~14k tokens across 3 mid-sized customers, likely due to the 12m stall.

carol_billing: 14k tokens is ~ $36 across those accounts — not critical, but we should ensure invoices don't undercount. what's the plan to backfill?

mike_prod: can we reprocess from the last checkpoint now that consumers are caught up? is there safe idempotent handling?

sam_sre: our pipeline supports replay from retained kafka for up to 24h. plan: run backfill job to re-ingest offsets 120-125 for partition 3 once we confirm no duplicates. job will dedupe by event-id.

jess_oncall: scheduling backfill now. starting at 02:25Z, targeting small batch and monitor.

incident-bot: Backfill job started by jess_oncall: job-id backfill-20260314-01 (offsets p3:120-125).

sam_sre: backfill running, no exceptions so far. throughput limited to avoid cascade.

olivia_support: letting the customers flagged in support know we’re investigating; will update with ETA for reconciliation.

carol_billing: once backfill completes, can we run a reconciliation and mark any invoice adjustments? prefer to batch small compensating charges rather than reopen invoices if possible.

mike_prod: agree. need to validate output parity before committing to billing adjustments. If less than $100 total across org, we absorb; otherwise propose credit on next invoice.

sam_sre: backfill finished at 02:33Z. processed offsets 120-125. reconciliation post-backfill shows delta reduced to 0 for the affected windows.

jess_oncall: great. confirming consumer lag cleared and checkpoint advanced.

incident-bot: Alert auto-resolved: metering.checkpoint_stall (PD-54321) at 2026-03-14T02:34:10Z

carol_billing: Verified token counts match expected now. no invoice adjustments required. will close internal ticket after a brief postmortem note.

mike_prod: nice work. pls file a short incident summary with root cause and action items (restarts -> consider automated consumer health probe and auto-restart policy).

jess_oncall: filing summary in #postmortems and creating a follow-up issue to add consumer readiness alert and automated graceful restart play.

olivia_support: updated customers we messaged: fixed, reconciliation complete.

sam_sre: notes for postmortem: root cause likely transient OffsetOutOfRange due to brief leader flaps on partition 3 during maintenance window. mitigation: tighten retention, add consumer group watchdog, and improve runbook for rolling restarts.

jess_oncall: handing off to next oncall @mike_prod for visibility. final: incident resolved, no billing impact, doc in progress. :party_popper:

mike_prod: ack handoff. thanks all.
